findings.summary: Abstract Wiener space constructs a rigorous Gaussian measure on a larger Banach space B from a smaller dense Hilbert space H. The classical example uses H as square-integrable derivative paths and B as continuous paths, yielding Wiener measure for Brownian motion. The Gaussian measure lives on B, while H, the Cameron-Martin space, has measure zero within B. The geometry of H controls the measure's properties, and the Cameron-Martin theorem describes how the measure changes under translations by elements of H. The construction provides necessary and sufficient conditions for the measure to extend from cylinder sets on H to a countably additive measure on B, making it the universal framework for Gaussian measures on infinite-dimensional Banach spaces.

mechanisms.title: Cylinder set extension from H to B
mechanisms.explanation: A cylinder set measure defined on the Hilbert space H of square-integrable derivatives is extended to the Banach space B of continuous paths. If B is sufficiently larger than H, this extension becomes a countably additive Gaussian measure on B, unlike on H where it fails due to infinite typical distance from the origin.

mechanisms.title: Cameron-Martin geometry governing measure properties
mechanisms.explanation: Although the Gaussian measure μ lives on the larger space B, it is the geometry of the Cameron-Martin space H that controls μ's properties. The Cameron-Martin theorem describes how the measure changes under translations by elements of H, and H's measure-zero status in B emphasizes that the measure resides on B, not H.
